memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Moses set aside three cities east of the Jordan, to which anyone who had killed a person could flee if they had unintentionally killed a neighbor without malice aforethought. They could flee into one of these cities and save their life. The cities were these: Bezer in the wilderness plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites. - Deut 4:41-43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of this great sermon, Moses does something very practical: he sets apart three cities of refuge east of the Jordan. Even before the people crossed into the main part of the land, Moses established these places of safety for anyone who killed another person accidentally. It is a striking picture of God's care running ahead of need — the refuge was prepared before anyone required it. God's provision was ready in advance.

We saw the beautiful meaning of the cities of refuge back in Numbers 35. Here we notice especially the timing: Moses set them apart proactively, ensuring that when tragedy struck, safety would already be in place. This reflects the heart of a God who prepares provision for His people before they even know they need it. His care is not reactive but foreseeing.

How comforting to serve a God who prepares refuge ahead of time. Before we stumble, before we cry out, God has already made a way of safety. His mercy runs ahead of our need. Just as these cities stood ready before anyone fled to them, God's provision for us is prepared in advance by His loving foresight.

This points us to Christ, our refuge, prepared before the foundation of the world. Scripture tells us that God's plan of salvation in Jesus was set in place before time began (1 Pet 1:20; Eph 1:4). Before we ever sinned, before we ever needed rescue, God had already prepared our refuge in His Son. When we flee to Christ, we run to a salvation that was ready and waiting for us all along. What a God — who prepares our refuge before we even know we need it. Run to Him, for safety is already prepared.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you that God prepares refuge ahead of your need?
2. Where have you seen God's provision ready before you even asked?
3. How does knowing Christ was prepared as your refuge before time began move your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, thank You that Your care runs ahead of my need, preparing refuge before I even know to seek it. Thank You that Christ, my refuge, was prepared before time began. Help me always to run to Him for safety. Amen.
